title: Comparison
subtitle: groter dan, even groot als, het grootst

explain.text: To compare two things add **-er** to the adjective and use **dan**: *Mijn huis is groter dan jouw huis.* The spelling rules are the same as for the plural: *groot → groter* (a long vowel keeps one letter), *dik → dikker* (a short vowel doubles the consonant).
If the adjective ends in **-r**, add **-der**: *duur → duurder*, *lekker → lekkerder*, *ver → verder*. Four common ones are irregular.

explain.nl: De trein is sneller dan de bus.
explain.en: The train is faster than the bus.

explain.nl: Ik drink liever thee dan koffie.
explain.en: I would rather drink tea than coffee.

items.explain: A long vowel keeps one letter in the open syllable: groter.

explain.text: The **superlative** adds **-st** (or **-ste** before a noun): *Dit is het grootste huis van de straat.* *Zij is de beste leraar.* Without a noun use **het + -st**: *Wie is het snelst?* The irregular ones: **goed – beter – best**, **veel – meer – meest**, **weinig – minder – minst**, **graag – liever – liefst**.
Adjectives ending in **-isch, -ief** and some long adjectives use **meer** and **meest**: *Dit antwoord is het meest logisch.*

explain.text: Use **dan** when things are different (*groter dan*). Use **als** when things are equal (*even groot als*). Mixing them up is a very common mistake.

items.text: Dit antwoord is het ___ logisch. (meest)
